description: Part IVA of the Indian Constitution, under Article 51A, enumerates the Fundamental Duties. These are moral and civic obligations for citizens, originally added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

sections.title: Historical Background and Origin
sections.description: Fundamental Duties were not part of the original Constitution. They were added later during the internal emergency to remind citizens that rights come with corresponding duties.

historical_events.significance: Set up by the Congress government during the Emergency to make recommendations about fundamental duties. The committee originally recommended the inclusion of 8 duties.

polity_articles.provision: Added a new Part IVA and Article 51A to the Constitution.
polity_articles.details: Introduced a list of 10 Fundamental Duties for the citizens of India.

polity_articles.provision: Added a new clause (k) to Article 51A.
polity_articles.details: Introduced the 11th Fundamental Duty, which makes it an obligation for parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6 to 14 years.

important_facts.fact: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

sections.title: Major Duties under Article 51A
sections.description: Article 51A currently lists 11 Fundamental Duties. From an examination perspective, the following specific clauses are highly important.

polity_articles.provision: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
polity_articles.details: Considered a primary Civic Duty of every Indian citizen.

polity_articles.provision: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
polity_articles.details: Regarded as one of the pre-eminent national obligations.

polity_articles.provision: To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.
polity_articles.details: A Moral Duty focusing on environmental conservation.

polity_articles.provision: To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
polity_articles.details: Aims to eradicate orthodoxy, superstitions, and promote rational thinking.

polity_articles.provision: To provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years.
polity_articles.details: Added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, complementing the Right to Education (Article 21A).

sections.title: Nature and Features
sections.description: Fundamental Duties share some functional similarities with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), particularly regarding their enforceability.

key_concepts.explanation: Fundamental Duties cannot be directly enforced by courts. The Constitution does not provide for direct legal enforcement or explicit penalties for their violation.
Unlike certain Fundamental Rights (such as Articles 14 or 21) which are available to foreigners, Fundamental Duties are restricted strictly to Indian citizens.
Although non-justiciable, Parliament is free to enforce them by passing suitable legislation to impose penalties or punishments for failure to fulfill any duty.

sections.title: Related Committees and Legal Provisions
sections.description: Various committees and existing laws provide statutory backing to the principles laid down in the Fundamental Duties.

key_associations.extra_info: This committee also recommended making the 'payment of taxes' a fundamental duty and imposing penalties for non-compliance, but these were not accepted by the government.
Identified existing legal provisions (like the Wildlife Protection Act and Representation of the People Act) for the implementation of some Fundamental Duties.

important_facts.fact: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 legally prevents disrespect to the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem, thereby providing statutory backing to Article 51A(a).
